Great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through your constraints and the draft architecture. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Key technical points from the call:
- Deployment mode: on-prem, air-gapped Private deployment (customer-managed network, no outbound internet).
- Short-term ask: hardware upgrade to support inference at target QPS (peak 150 concurrent sessions); current hardware underprovisioned.
- Preferred timeline: runway for upgrades in May maintenance window; production cutover late June.

Immediate open items we agreed to confirm:
1) GPU target per rack (you mentioned 4x A100 80GB per rack as a starting point; please confirm).
2) Available NVMe / local disk per node (we need 8TB NVMe per node minimum for KV cache + swap).
3) Strict maintenance windows and blackout dates for air-gapped syncs.
4) Onsite access and logistics for appliance install vs. remote engineers (airgap will require an onsite media handoff).

Attachments: redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.xlsx (hardware + network checklist), airgap-install-runbook.pdf (high-level install steps), hardware-upgrade-checklist.docx.

Marissa -

Notes from an ops/engineering perspective (draft):
- NVMe requirement: 8TB per node is the safe minimum for KV cache + local swap; if you expect large context loads (20k tokens), we should size up to 12TB. 4TB will throttle throughput and increase network I/O.
- Storage durability: use RAID1 for OS partition and keep NVMe as raw devices for cache performance; plan for hot-swap of NVMe modules where possible.
- Airgap media process: we'll provide a signed SHA256 manifest for each artifact. Customer to provide physical media ingestion endpoint in the server room; Redwood engineer will hand off sealed media.
- OS/firmware updates: we recommend a staged approach - apply firmware only during scheduled maintenance windows with image rollback available. We build bootable recovery media as part of the install.
- Offline model patching: typical maintenance downtime 20-45 minutes for model swap if KV warmup is not required. With pre-warmed cache images staged locally, downtime can be reduced to <10 minutes.

Action items for our team: I'll draft the offline-ops runbook and an upgrade sequence (pre-checks, backup, apply, validate, rollback). Will circulate by Mon 2027-04-05. Also need exact NVMe upgrade procurement timeline from John/procurement.

-Vivek
